title: Design and analysis of recurrent neural network models with non-linear activation functions for solving time-varying quadratic programming problems
model_class: finite-time ZNN with non-linear / non-convex activations (NPZNN, SSZNN, CZNN, SZNN)
problem_class: TVQP with equality and bound constraints
ev_R3: "For the solutions to these special equations, the ODE solver in Matlab is utilised in the simulation experiment." (Sec. 4; solver not named)
ev_R4: no step size or tolerance reported (Sec. 4)
ev_R6: "Simulative results are illustrated in Figure 1 with the parameters chosen as γ = 2" for GNN, ZNN, SBPZNN, SSZNN and CZNN (Sec. 4.1)
solver_detail: unnamed MATLAB ODE-suite solver (coded adaptive), tolerances not stated
notes: Wiley HTML full text. Single benchmark TVQP (18) (x in R^2, one equality, four bound rows; augmented state m+n+p = 7). Baselines: GNN [30], original ZNN [24], SBPZNN model (6) re-simulated (Fig. 1, Table 1); NPZNN/SSZNN/CZNN/SZNN are the proposed variants. Same γ=2 across different activations, no fairness discussion -> R6=no. Finite-time bounds tc given (Theorems 3-5) but Table 1 convergence times (2.5/1.8/1 s) are not compared with them -> R10=no. R3 borderline: 'the ODE solver in Matlab' coded adaptive because MATLAB's ode suite is adaptive; could be read as not-stated.

title: An advanced bionic knee joint mechanism with neural network controller
problem_class: bionic knee joint (2-DOF tensegrity mechanism) trajectory control for rehabilitation
ev_R3: no solver/step statement; "through the experiments, the effectiveness of the bionic knee joint is verified under the interference of noise items" (Sec. 5; simulations of the dynamics model)
ev_R4: no step size or tolerance reported (Sec. 5)
ev_R6: "the PID algorithm is used as the controller to control the bionic knee joint dynamics model in the contrast experiments" (Sec. 5.2); no NTZNN (β, λ) or PID gains reported
ev_R11: "The original contributions presented in the study are included in the article/supplementary material, further inquiries can be directed to the corresponding author." (Data availability)
solver_detail: not stated (desired trajectory fitted with ADAMS)
notes: Frontiers HTML full text. One tracking task (desired θ, γ trajectories) under three rehabilitation-stage knee torques (-40, 150, 0 N·m) treated as disturbance conditions of the same problem -> R1=1; 2 generalized coordinates -> R2=2. Single baseline PID, gains of neither controller reported -> R6 unclear. Noise: mixed ε(t)=η+κt+μ(t) (constant+linear+random). 'Experiments' are simulations of the Lagrangian model (conclusion says 'simulations'), no prototype -> R12=no. Laplace-based asymptotic convergence only (R10 NA).

title: Computing quaternion matrix pseudoinverse with zeroing neural networks
model_class: ZNN (linear; quaternion-domain, complex- and real-representation models ZNNQ/ZNNQC/ZNNQR)
problem_class: time-varying quaternion matrix pseudoinverse; robot kinematic control (3-link planar manipulator)
ev_R3: "the NSs have used the MATLAB ode15s solver in the time interval [0, 10] using the default double precision arithmetic (eps = 2.22 · 10^-16)" (Sec. 5)
ev_R4: no RelTol/AbsTol or step; only machine precision quoted and "the minimum value in all of the figures of this section are mostly of order 10^-5" (Sec. 5)
ev_R6: NA: only the paper's own three formulations (ZNNQ, ZNNQC, ZNNQR) are compared, all with "λ is used with values of 10 and 100" (Sec. 5)
notes: AIMS PDF (downloaded to the coder's scratchpad; journal HTML not used). Four numerical simulations: quaternion 3x3 singular, 4x2 full rank, 3x6 and 12x4 rank deficient (R2=12; real representation 48x16), plus 3-link planar manipulator 'M'-path tracking (simulation). No external baseline (R7=0), no noise, exponential convergence only. Regularisation γ=1e-8 for rank-deficient cases.

problem_class: time-varying constrained optimisation; microgrid economic dispatch (application)
